title: Letting agents urged to assess landlord profitability
summary:
Letting agents are being advised to evaluate landlord clients based on profitability rather than portfolio size, as regulatory pressures and operational costs reshape the sector's economics. Industry analysis shows that 'cost to serve' metrics and client quality directly impact both current profitability and future business sale values.

title: UK housing market remains subdued with weak demand, RICS reports
summary:
The UK property market continues to show limited signs of recovery, with buyer demand and agreed sales remaining unchanged in July, according to the latest RICS residential market survey. New buyer enquiries recorded a net balance of -28%, matching June's figure.

The post UK housing market remains subdued with weak demand, RICS reports appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Stamp duty costs double over decade despite modest price growth
summary:
Stamp duty on an average property purchase in Britain has increased by more than 100% over the past decade, while house prices rose by just 28%, according to analysis by accountancy firm Blick Rothenberg. The firm's research indicates that frozen tax thresholds have created a fiscal drag, pushing a larger proportion of each transaction into higher tax bands.

title: Modon reports AED 26bn in H1 2026 property sales
summary:
Abu Dhabi-based developer Modon has reported AED 26 billion in property sales for the first half of 2026, with approximately AED 23 billion generated in Abu Dhabi alone. Around AED 13 billion came from the Hudayriyat Golf Estates launch.

title: Property agents deploy AI to handle AI-generated complaints
summary:
Property agents are increasingly using artificial intelligence to process tenant complaints that have themselves been generated using AI tools, according to industry professionals. The development is creating new operational challenges for letting agencies.

title: Estate agencies warned on cash flow as profits decline
summary:
Estate agency businesses are facing mounting financial pressure as recent profit reports reveal declining margins, with industry analysts warning that cash flow management will determine which firms survive the current downturn. The fixed cost structure of agency operations means revenue declines can eliminate profits entirely.

title: Ground rent cap faces implementation challenges
summary:
The UK government's planned cap on ground rents at £250 annually is set to affect approximately 3.8 million residential leasehold properties in England and Wales, with implementation expected in late 2028.

title: Cottage buyer interest falls 32% since 2023
summary:
Buyer interest in English countryside cottages has declined by 32% since the start of 2023, according to new data from property portal Zoopla. The average cottage price currently stands at £321,641, representing a 0.3% decline compared to August 2025.

title: Rental void periods decline to 21 days after legislation
summary:
Rental void periods across England have decreased to an average of 21 days in June, down from 24 days in May when the Renters' Rights Act came into force. The reduction suggests landlords are adjusting to new legislative requirements, though voids remain longer than the previous year.

title: New-build developers resist price cuts despite sales slowdown
summary:
Housebuilders are maintaining asking prices despite around one in eight new-build properties remaining unsold after six months on the market, according to analysis by specialist lender Octane Capital. The data shows that developers are prioritising profitability over sales velocity, with only 14.5% of properties seeing price reductions.
